clause_that_reaches_it: Two situations that merely look alike may legitimately differ
why_in_scope: The question 'I have named this image twice in ## Images — do I get one picture or two?' is answered in two places, and differently: the dash loop keeps both, the inline sweep drops the second. That is enough for the ruling to reach. It resolves to COMPLIES on the clause's own escape: the two situations only look alike. A dash item is an explicit entry in the card's image list; the inline sweep is a salvage pass over loose prose in that section, and it dedupes against the authoritative list precisely so a caption-style `![](x)` beside an already-listed picture does not double it. Unifying the two rules would be an improvement, not a correction.
